title: How many bug triagers a browser vendor needs for the first quarter of 2027, its first on a new tracker, when every one of the quarter's releases ships on Patch Tuesday and meets the Windows restart wave in its own release week
subdomain: feature-adoption-diffusion-modeling (a desktop browser's releases reaching its installs: each install takes an update at its next restart and most Windows installs restart in the two days after Patch Tuesday, so a release's first-week reach and the first-use reports that follow are set by where it sits in the monthly restart cycle)
prompt_shape: a committed headcount (triagers, rounded up from the busiest week's forecast at 120 items per triager-week) with the busiest week's forecast to the nearest 100, a table of the parallel run's four weeks (triage items with no triage action within 24 hours of filing, triage items closed by the run's end), a table of the eight component groups (triage items that arrived in each group's components), and a chart of the weekly figures

sources.origin: constructed for this task by task162/generator/build.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional Tampere browser vendor, in the layouts of a Bugzilla-style CSV bug export, a Jira-style REST search export with changelogs, a public data portal's daily series, office workbooks and documents, a release calendar PDF and a mail thread; no real organisation's records or person is depicted.
